clauses.text:
Executive Order 11343
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE THE DISPUTES
BETWEEN THE LONG ISLAND RAIL ROAD AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS, three disputes exist between The Long Island Rail  
Road, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the  
Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, International Brotherhood of  
Electrical Workers and International Association of Machinists and  
Aerospace Workers, labor organizations;  and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce  
to such a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essen­
tial transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Section 10 of the Railway Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I hereby 
create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to investigate  
these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or other­
wise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
these disputes within 30 days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by  
The Long Island Rail Road, or by its employees, in the conditions out  
< ? f which these disputes arose.

versions.research_rationale:
EO 11343 (1967-04-12, 32 FR 6085) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate three disputes between the Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers and the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11343.txt, 32 FR 6085, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within 30 days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11343 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

whole_order_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11343 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
